title: Nijigahara Holograph
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Fifth-grader Arie Kimura tells classmates a fairy tale about a girl sent by God who is sacrificed to a monster in the Nijigahara tunnel; the bullied Arie is then pushed down a well by seven classmates and left in a coma. Told out of order across two timelines, the single volume follows those children as damaged adults, amid swarms of butterflies, hidden abuse and spiralling violence.
life_message: It offers no settled good life; it shows how cruelty and silence among children and adults echo for years.

content.note: Stabbing, a blinding, a murder by house fire, a killing with an umbrella (Wikipedia; AniList Crime, Tragedy).
Psychological horror; Publishers Weekly called it a 'dark and twisted psychological horror story' (Wikipedia; AniList Denpa).
Arie raped as a child by her father and by Makoto; an attempted assault; nudity (Wikipedia; MangaUpdates Rape, Nudity; AniList Rape). Explicitness to verify.
Harsh speech among bullies; level not documented (to verify).
Suicidal Suzuki, lifelong guilt and trauma, a teacher who turns abusive (Wikipedia; AniList Suicide, Bullying; MangaUpdates Bullying).
Children push a classmate down a well as a 'sacrifice'; adults call it an accident (Wikipedia; AniList Bullying).

dominant: Trauma and guilt; nihilistic cycles of violence; sacrifice myth

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Kohta answers wrongs with personal violence; others hide guilt.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Adult authorities fail; no order is celebrated or rejected.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family abuse and class cruelty both corrode; neither is upheld.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Teacher-pupil hierarchy present but shown hollow.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Folk sacrifice myth drives children; no religious answer offered.

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Characters are absorbed by survival and fear rather than self-expression.

folkways.japan: Classroom bullying (ijime) and the group's scapegoating of an outsider reflect a widely discussed Japanese school concern, here treated as horror.

delivery.evidence: Entry: two out-of-order timelines withhold comfort and leave meaning to the reader (to verify)
delivery.note: It states no lesson; readers piece together how cruelty and silence echo.

winners_losers: No one wins; abusers and bystanders alike are haunted. Sympathy goes to Arie, the sacrificed child, and the story withholds comfort.
